API authentication tokens are validated as group_hash == SHA1(ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT + ':' + user_id).hexdigest(). ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT is hardcoded in pygoat/settings.py (committed to the repo), and SHA1 is unsalted/fast — anyone with the salt can forge a valid token for any user id and impersonate them (including admins) via the API.

Django SECRET_KEY is hardcoded in source ('+f0x#go-9e-qd(mq0pdn9ma*ls!h+4uy2hcofnep!o0=ow=ewn'). Anyone with repository access can forge signed sessions, password-reset tokens, and other cryptographic signatures.
DEBUG = True. If deployed, Django debug pages leak settings, environment variables, stack traces and source code, and enable the verbose error handler.
ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['*'] accepts any Host header, enabling HTTP Host header attacks (cache poisoning, malicious password-reset link generation, etc.).

KEY = b'12345678910111212345678910111212' is a hardcoded, single AES key (used in app/models/utils.py Encryption with AES-CBC) protecting SSNs and bank account numbers for all users. A hardcoded, guessable, globally shared key defeats the encryption entirely.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT = 'S4828341189aefiasd#ASDF' is hardcoded in source. It is the sole secret behind the SHA1-based API token scheme in app/views/api/users/views.py, so its disclosure lets anyone forge API tokens for arbitrary users.
